$comment: AM2.6: colour re-ranking on real SigLIP 2 weights through the Visual Embed worker (visual.embed shots with a region, visual.text palette prompts), scored with the shipped rule. Produced by workers/visual-embed/tools/colour_rerank_eval.py on the maintainer's M1 Pro, one job at a time under workers/smart-mask/spike/watchdog.py's limits (8 GiB footprint, start at >= 40% free, abort on > 1 GiB swap growth). Not run in CI: it needs the pinned weights.

cropSet.synthetic: 48 frames at 640x360 (6 backgrounds: grass, sky, asphalt, off-white wall, dark room, multi-hue clutter; x 2 nouns: car, ball; x 4), three objects per frame in three distinct palette colours drawn by seed, flat-shaded with a vertical light gradient and noise (cars have pale windows and black wheels), encoded H.264 yuv420p crf 18 all-intra and decoded by the worker's OpenCV path; crops are the object's box plus 6% per side, like a detector box. Requests: every colour on the frame (must pick that object) and every colour not on it (must ask): 144 + 432 per set.
cropSet.realFootage: tests/fixtures/mission/broll/b4-1080p-50s.mp4 at 2.0 s (fetched fixture, not in git): hand-boxed purple monitor, black microphone, white lamp bulb (lit warm); noun 'object'; 3 present + 9 absent requests. The mission photos were not used (personal documents); the other clips hold no boxable coloured objects.
cropSet.caveat: 'silver' is rendered flat (190,192,198) with no metallic sheen; SigLIP reads every such crop as white or grey, so silver ground truth here is harder than a real silver car.

rules.am2.5-share: AM2.5 as shipped: the named colour's softmax share (T 0.01) over the 12 palette prompts; resolver picks the top candidate when >= 0.5 and >= 1.25x the runner-up.
rules.am2.6: Shipped now (colour-rerank.ts colourEvidence): head to head, named / (named + strongest other colour); undecided (held just under 0.5) when the named colour is not strictly ahead, or when an achromatic request (white, grey, silver, black) finds >= 0.1 of the crop on another achromatic word. Same resolver rule. Designed on the reported seed; the held-out seed was generated after.

before.what: HEAD before AM2.6: two worker processes per colour request (visual.embed crops, then visual.text prompts), each loading BOTH towers on CoreML and, with no cache folder passed, re-encoding the 43-sentence prompt bank.
before.result: did not complete under the watchdog, twice: killed 18.3 s into the first of the two processes at a 7.50 GiB footprint (swap +1.31 GiB); an earlier single-process load of both towers reached 7.41 GiB (swap +2.90 GiB).

newPackOldHost.what: CPU provider and lazy towers, still two processes and no cache folder

after.what: CPU provider, lazy towers, host passes FRAMEPILOT_CAPABILITY_PACK_CACHE and keeps the palette prompt vectors per pack release: the first request per noun runs visual.embed + visual.text; later ones only visual.embed, vision tower only

parity.textCpuVsCoreml: not measured: the CoreML text load was stopped by the watchdog (7.77 GiB, swap +1.18 GiB)

verdict: AM2.7: with the engine's colour measurement beside SigLIP, every AM5 gate is met on the two calibration sets, the three real crops and the held-out set (seed 424242, generated and scored after the thresholds were frozen): held-out targets 144/144, white/grey/silver/black 52/52, confident-wrong 0; SigLIP alone resolves 109/144 of the same targets. Caveat: the crops are flat renderings (no metallic sheen, no coloured light, no shadowed whites) and real footage is three objects; 'silver' is separated from 'grey' by lightness alone.

am2.7.$comment: AM2.7: SigLIP 2 (real vectors, as AM2.6 measured them) plus the engine's CIELAB measurement of each crop (framepilot_engine/masking/crop_colour.py, decoded by the export's ffmpeg). Scored by engine/python/tests/colour_rerank_replay.py from colour-rerank-replay.json; CI re-derives these numbers and re-measures the synthetic crops (test_colour_rerank_replay.py).

measurement.region: detection box weighted (1 - (u^2 + v^2))^2: 1 at the centre, 0 on the inscribed ellipse and in the corners; no matte (none exists at find time)
measurement.colourPipeline: export ffmpeg (find_export_ffmpeg), scale + bicubic + rgb24: the source's tagged BT.601/BT.709 matrix and range; R'G'B' read as sRGB, CIELAB D65
measurement.neutralLightness: dominant L* of the neutral pixels: weighted median within 12 L* of the densest tone (so glass and tyres do not drag a white body to grey)

am2.7.rule: Pick only when both signals agree. Chromatic colour: SigLIP's decisive pick (AM2.6 evidence >= 0.5 and >= 1.25x runner-up) whose crop measures chromatic. White, grey, silver, black: the single crop measured in that class, with no crop in a band next to it and none mixed or unmeasured; SigLIP's top colour for it must be neutral and at most one step away on black-grey-silver-white, and SigLIP must not name the colour for a rival while not naming it for the pick. Otherwise every candidate is held under the resolver's floor and the editor is asked.

thresholds.fitRule: per neighbouring pair, the middle half of the calibration gap is a dead band (asks); frozen = fit rounded (shares 2 dp, L* 1 dp) before the held-out set was scored

am2.6Verdict: Real crops do not meet the AM5 accuracy or unnecessary-ask gates with either rule; those gates are not lowered. The AM2.5 rule made confident-wrong picks on real weights (5 and 7 of 432 absent-colour requests: 'the white/grey X' taking a silver one); the AM2.6 rule makes none on either set or the real crops. Chromatic colours are 101/101 on both sets; white, grey, black and silver ask far more often (silver never resolves on these renderings).
